sections.title: Replacing Relative Clauses with Pre-Nominal Participles
sections.content: Where English places relative clauses AFTER a noun ('the avenue that connects the city center with the City Park'), Hungarian formal and architectural prose places the entire modifier phrase BEFORE the head noun using the active present participle (-ó/-ő): a belvárost a Városligettel összekötő Andrássy út.

sections.title: Internal Word Order of the Participial Phrase
sections.content: Inside the pre-nominal participial phrase, all objects, adverbs, and case-marked complements precede the -ó/-ő participle, and the participle itself stands immediately before the head noun it modifies: [Article of Head Noun] + [Complements/Objects] + [Participle in -ó/-ő] + [Head Noun].

items.spanish: A belvárost a Városligettel összekötő Andrássy út európai léptékű sugárút lett.
items.english: Andrássy Avenue, connecting the downtown with the City Park, became a boulevard on a European scale.

items.spanish: Az Andrássy út burkolata alatt futó földalatti vasút 1896-ra készült el.
items.english: The underground railway running beneath the pavement of Andrássy Avenue was completed by 1896.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Notice the initial definite article belongs to the head noun at the end of the phrase: [A] [belvárost a Városligettel összekötő] [Andrássy út].
